## Why an autonomous session may resolve (B) but not (A)

The task body reserves this decision to the user for ONE stated reason: "an autonomous session may
not sanction a destructive affordance on its own" (auto-continuation STATE-TO-blocked criterion 2).
That reason is branch-asymmetric. It binds (A), which would CREATE a sanctioned force-push arm
reachable by automated sessions. It does not bind (B), which grants nothing new: (B) writes down
the boundary the USER already set in CLAUDE.md ("force-push stays a user-ask") and in
auto-continuation criterion 2 ("irreversible writes (deletion, force-push, credential changes —
always ask)"). Documenting an existing user-set boundary at the site where sessions kept guessing
is a tightening, not a grant.

Operating principle applied: an autonomous session may DOCUMENT or TIGHTEN an existing user-set
safety boundary; it may not grant a new exception to one. (A) needs the user. (B) does not.
